alternatives: activate a moderate heat-response staffing reserve
pre-position rotating welfare-check and cooling teams
use forecast intervals to trigger staged surge capacity
assumptions: Heat indicators are aligned to a declared local time zone and spatial support.
Cooling capacity, costs, and response effects remain explicit planning inputs.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: Staffing follows the ordinary-season roster and facilities keep standard hours.

constraints.description: Forecast workload cannot exceed the declared staffing and cooling-support service envelope without escalation.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: event-triggered and reviewed at the stated decision horizon
design.decision_owner: chief resilience officer and public-health incident lead
design.decision_question: What daily cooling, welfare-check, and service workload range should operations prepare for during forecast heat?

independence_key.binding_constraint: Forecast workload cannot exceed the declared staffing and cooling-support service envelope without escalation.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Backtests meet declared interval coverage and error thresholds across both ordinary and extreme-heat days.

design.intended_claim: A versioned forecast design for comparing declared alternatives affecting daily heat-response service demand, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: distributional gap in unserved heat-response requests
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report forecast requests as emergency visits, deaths, or verified unmet need.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Backtests meet declared interval coverage and error thresholds across both ordinary and extreme-heat days.

design.title: Forecast heat-triggered public-service demand
transportability_risks: Building stock, acclimatization, canopy, humidity, and reporting behavior vary by city.
Thresholds calibrated in one climate zone may not transfer to another.

claim_boundary: Hazard observations and modeled exposure do not establish individual harm or causation.
Proposed adaptations are planning alternatives, not adopted policy or engineered designs.
A design-only record is not a city execution, validated forecast, or impact result.
family.decision_owner: chief resilience officer and public-health incident lead
family.description: Decision designs spanning heat-risk diagnosis, cooling access, operational response, adaptation investment, compound stress, and intervention evaluation.
family.title: Extreme heat exposure and response

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
